transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?
I came in because I’ve been feeling low for a long time. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already on me, even before I get to the clinic, and it just kind of stays with me through the day.
Can you tell me roughly how long you've been feeling this way—has it been weeks, months, or even years?
About two years and two months now. It really started after the clinic staffing changed and my schedule began rotating all over the place.
Over these past two years, have you ever had a distinct period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any stretch where I felt unusually up or had a lot more energy like that.

Over these two years, has your mood stayed at a fairly steady low level, or have there been times when it became much more severe—where you couldn't function at work or in daily life—compared to other times?

It’s been pretty consistently low, but it has gotten bad enough that I’m not keeping up. My supervisor put me on a performance plan because I made too many mistakes doing intakes. And outside work, I’ve stopped going to basketball or finishing the little electronics projects I used to do with friends. I just can’t keep up with anything beyond work anymore.

During these two years, has there been any period of at least two weeks when your low mood was noticeably worse—for example, involving thoughts of not wanting to be alive, major changes in your appetite or weight, or a near-total inability to feel interest in anything?
I’m not really sure. It’s felt low for a long time, but I can’t point to a separate two-week stretch where it was clearly worse than the rest.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed any change in your sleep—such as difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a real change in my sleep lately.
Have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or weight over the past couple of weeks?
I don’t think so. My appetite and weight seem about the same lately.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressive mood persisting for over two years without a clear superimposed major depressive episode (no distinct 2-week period with worsened mood, suicidal ideation, or appetite/sleep changes). There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, ruling out bipolar disorder. The chronicity, absence of episodic major depressive features, and associated functional impairment (performance plan at work, withdrawal from hobbies and social activities) are consistent with Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia, F34.1) rather than Major Depressive Disorder or an adjustment disorder, given the duration exceeds two years and stressor (schedule change) predates but does not fully explain the chronic course.
